conversation:
User request: Fix three UX rough edges in how StepKit spawns an interactive CLI agent for a workflow step (the code path used by grill-it-away's grilling step, and any other step using `mode: "interactive"`), discovered from a live test transcript of `stepkit grill-it-away`.

The assistant researched the current implementation before proposing anything and confirmed the following about existing behavior, centered on `packages/core/src/agent-execution/interactive-agent/run-interactive-agent-command/run-interactive-agent-command.ts`:

- `runInteractiveAgentTarget` resolves either a registry provider (e.g. `claude`) or a custom provider, and in both branches spawns the agent CLI process with `cwd: options.runDir` (the run root, e.g. `.stepkit/runs/grill-it-away-<timestamp>-<hash>/`), NOT the step's own directory.
- `buildInteractivePrompt` constructs a single string: a harness preamble (a line naming the step directory, the full JSON output schema for the step, and literal `stepkit continue` usage instructions) followed by `"## Original prompt"` and the step's actual rendered role prompt (e.g. "You are the interactive front door for starting a new StepKit feature. Open by asking the user what they want to build."). This single combined string is passed as `request.prompt` to the provider adapter's `runInteractive`.
- `packages/core/src/known-cli-providers/providers/claude/claude-provider.ts`'s `runInteractive` (the interactive-mode adapter for the built-in `claude` provider) pushes `request.prompt` as a positional CLI argument to the `claude` binary and inherits stdio - Claude Code echoes that whole positional argument as the session's first user turn, and does NOT include `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (unlike the sibling non-interactive "working" path, `buildClaudeWorkingArgs`, which always includes that flag unconditionally).
- Separately, `stepkit continue --json-file <path>`'s implementation in `packages/cli/src/internals/commands/continue/continue-command.ts` resolves any relative `--json-file`/`--session-file` path via `resolveAgainstStepDir`, against `interactive.stepDir` - the step directory (`runDir/steps/0001-<step-id>/`), one level deeper than the process's actual `runDir` cwd.

In the observed test transcript, this combination produced exactly the confusion reported: the agent saw the full schema/instructions dump as if it were a chat message, was not running with permissions bypassed (so tool calls needed manual approval), and because its cwd (`runDir`) did not match the base `stepkit continue` resolves relative paths against (`stepDir`), a bare `stepkit continue --json-file output.json` failed with ENOENT, and the agent's self-correction attempt (moving the file into `steps/0001-grill/` and re-running with that as the path) produced a doubled `steps/0001-grill/steps/0001-grill/output.json` path, since `resolveAgainstStepDir` always prepends the already-deeper `stepDir`.

Through discussion with the user (including confirming via `claude --help` that `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--append-system-prompt-file <path>` are both real, currently-supported flags on the `claude` CLI), the following design decisions were made:

1. Permission bypass becomes the default for interactive agent steps, not opt-in. Add `permissionMode?: "bypass" | "prompt"` to `StepKitAgentTarget` (in `packages/core/src/agent-targeting/targeting.types.ts`) and the same optional field to `ProviderInteractiveRequest` (in `packages/core/src/known-cli-providers/registry/provider-registry.types.ts`). Undefined/absent means `"bypass"` - the new default. A user must explicitly set `"permissionMode": "prompt"` on an agent target entry in `.stepkit/config.json` (e.g. `{ "provider": "claude", "permissionMode": "prompt" }` under an `agents` mapping) to restore today's per-tool confirmation behavior. `runInteractiveAgentTarget` spreads `options.target.permissionMode` into the registry provider's `runInteractive` call the same way `model` is already spread. `claude-provider.ts`'s `runInteractive` pushes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` unless `request.permissionMode === "prompt"`, bringing the interactive path in line with the non-interactive working path's existing unconditional behavior. This is scoped to the built-in `claude` registry adapter only for now - `gemini`/`pi` adapters explicitly document that they only implement CLI flags confirmed against a real binary (see the existing `thinking`-flag no-op precedent in `gemini-provider.ts`), so `permissionMode` should be a harmless no-op there rather than a guessed flag. Custom providers (the `customProviders` escape hatch in config) are unaffected since they already fully control their own `interactiveArgs`.

2. Nothing should be shown in the visible transcript until the agent itself speaks first - not the schema/instructions preamble, and not the role prompt either (both are equally "plumbing" from the human's point of view; the agent's own first reply, e.g. "What would you like to build?", is what the human should see first). Implementation: `prepareInteractiveArtifacts` writes the full current `buildInteractivePrompt(...)` output (preamble + `## Original prompt` + rendered role prompt) to `options.files.promptFile` - a path that already exists in `StepArtifactPaths`/`interactive.json` metadata but is currently never actually written to disk for registry providers. `runInteractiveAgentTarget`'s registry-provider branch then passes a new field, `systemPromptFile: files.promptFile`, to `provider.runInteractive(...)`, and `ProviderInteractiveRequest` gains this as an optional field. `request.prompt` remains the fallback full combined text, unchanged, for any adapter that doesn't understand `systemPromptFile` (gemini, pi, and the custom-provider path all keep working exactly as today, since none has a confirmed system-prompt flag). In `claude-provider.ts`'s `runInteractive`: when `request.systemPromptFile` is set, push `--append-system-prompt-file <path>` (which appends to Claude Code's own default system prompt rather than replacing it, so its normal tool-use instructions are preserved) and push NO positional prompt argument at all - the session starts bare and the model's first turn is expected to be driven entirely by the appended system-prompt instructions (e.g. "Open by asking the user what they want to build"). When `systemPromptFile` is absent, fall back to today's unchanged behavior (`args.push(request.prompt)`). This rests on one assumption worth confirming with a real run early during implementation: that Claude Code, launched this way with no positional prompt, has the model take the first turn on its own rather than sitting idle waiting for human input first. If that assumption turns out to be false in practice, the documented fallback is to keep a minimal, constant, non-schema visible kickoff line (something like a fixed "Begin." trigger) instead of reverting to the current per-step schema dump.

3. Fix the cwd / `stepkit continue` path mismatch by changing the interactive child process's cwd from `options.runDir` to `files.stepDir` in both spawn sites inside `runInteractiveAgentTarget` (the registry-provider branch and the custom-provider branch), so the agent's actual working directory matches the base `stepkit continue`'s `resolveAgainstStepDir` already resolves relative paths against. Once cwd equals stepDir, `stepkit continue --json-file output.json` and `stepkit continue --session-file session-description.md` both just work with bare filenames and no path arithmetic. Update `buildInteractivePrompt`'s preamble text to match: drop the `Step directory: <relative-path>` line entirely (no longer meaningful - it now is the current directory), and reword "Write a dense session description to session-description.md in the step directory" to "...in the current directory". No other runtime code depends on the child process's cwd being `runDir` specifically - `prepareInteractiveArtifacts`, `readCompletedOutput`, and the completion-watcher all already address files via their fully-resolved absolute paths (`files.stepDir`, `files.interactiveFile`, etc.), never via `process.cwd()`.

4. Test coverage to add/update as part of this change: in `run-interactive-agent-command.test.ts`, update spawn-call assertions that currently expect `cwd: options.runDir` to expect `files.stepDir` instead; update prompt-string assertions (e.g. checks against `"## Original prompt\n..."` or the `Step directory:` line) to reflect that this content now lives in the written `systemPromptFile`, not the CLI's positional prompt; add coverage for `systemPromptFile` being written and passed through, and for `permissionMode` propagation including the default-is-bypass case. In `claude-provider.test.ts`, update the existing "launches with inherited stdio and --model but no dangerous-permissions flag" test since the default now needs the flag present; add a case for `permissionMode: "prompt"` omitting the flag; add a case for `systemPromptFile` producing `--append-system-prompt-file <path>` with no positional prompt argument pushed. `continue-command.test.ts`'s existing tests already construct `stepDir`/`runDir` explicitly and should continue to pass unchanged, since they don't depend on the interactive child's actual process cwd, but are worth a quick pass to confirm no implicit assumption breaks.

The user explicitly asked to move straight to implementation via the take-it-away pipeline once this design was written up, rather than have the assistant implement it directly in the current conversation.
